summary:
The Irony and The Ecstasy
VLCC Rates: Red Hot to Ice Hot The last long weekend of summer is setting in today and ironically VLCC rates, normally known for their ability to rise after the three month summer lull have just started to fall. While VLCC rates have begun to cool off this month, they are still above historical averages. Between Russian oil company Yukos' financial woes, Iraqi rebel habits of pipeline sabotage and high worldwide oil production, VLCC rates have barely had time to catch their breath, to the benefit of owners.

children.title: Strong Oil Demand
children.summary: The International Energy Agency predicts that demand for oil will reach 82.5 million barrels per day in the 4th quarter of 2004, the highest growth rate in 10 years. The agency predicts that demand will grow by an additional 700,000 barrels per day in 2005.

children.title: Shifting Trading Patterns?
children.summary: All these explanations on why rates should be robust are not supported by fixture activity, which, in general, has been declining in 2004. Even the key Arabian Gulf trade lacks luster.

children.title: Monthly VLCC Fixture Activity
children.summary: Fixture activity, while up overall, has declined in recent months on a month- to-month basis. This is not a sign of an overly robust market.

children.title: What Does This Mean?
children.summary: Yes, there are overall more vessels being fixed indicating higher levels of export. Yes, there is a great deal of anxiety in the market with Yukos and Iraq currently at the head of the list.
